thesis: Preston Byrne argues that Bitcoin functions as a 'Nakamoto scheme,' which is a digital-age variation of a Ponzi or pyramid scheme because its value relies entirely on new investor funds rather than underlying rights or obligations. He explains that while the scheme automates peer-to-peer cash interactions, the introduction of speculation causes it to operate like a classical Ponzi scheme where value is derived solely from the aggregate demand of new entrants.
